title: Diagnose a contaminated culture from clues
summary: Inspect and quarantine five synthetic flasks, select microbial/mycoplasma/STR evidence, choose dispositions, interpret linked-record clues to trace source hypotheses and complete an incident handoff.
scenario: Five synthetic flasks P, Q, R, S and T carry the same claimed line label. Seeded runs permute one visible bacterial pattern, one visible fungal pattern, one clear mycoplasma-positive flask and one clear STR-mismatched flask, and one clear reviewed-match flask. No assignment is visible initially. Inspect and quarantine the full five-flask linked set before any test, disposition or antibiotic intervention; clear appearance cannot substitute for dedicated mycoplasma evidence, and identity remains unresolved until STR evidence is revealed. All organisms, profiles and records are synthetic. Inspection reveals a per-flask synthetic linked-record bundle with investigative leads and competing hypotheses, not the condition assignment or expected source.
guided_steps: Inspect flasks P, Q, R, S and T. Turbidity/pH/rods and filaments/micro-colonies are clue patterns, not species names; clear flasks remain unresolved. Read the linked-record bundle revealed by each inspection; its clue and competing hypotheses are investigative evidence, not a hidden-condition or route reveal.

Inspect and quarantine all five linked flasks before ordering any test, recording any disposition or attempting antibiotic intervention. The engine retains per-flask inspection/quarantine checks and also rejects early action while any linked flask is pending.
Use Gram stain for the bacterial-pattern flask and fungal subculture for the fungal-pattern flask. These broad tests support, but do not speciate, the visible pattern.
Order a dedicated mycoplasma PCR, culture or DNA-stain test for all three clear flasks. The scenario displays valid controls; negative appearance, Gram stain and STR are not substitutes.
Order STR profiles for all three clear flasks and record match or mismatch only after reviewing the synthetic reference and sample allele calls.

Choose sealed decontaminated discard for confirmed visible contamination and mycoplasma-positive culture, identity hold for mismatch, and reviewed release only for the clear mycoplasma-negative STR match.
Antibiotic attempts do not sterilise or release a flask and fail the no-masking checkpoint. Use an evidence-based disposition instead.

After each disposition, use that flask's already revealed linked-record bundle to weigh the source choices against competing hypotheses. Select shared medium, shared incubator, incoming shipment, shared pipette/label-handling, no route identified or unresolved as the evidence warrants. A record clue supports an investigation; it does not prove the hidden condition or route.
Complete an all-linked-flasks handoff with tests/controls, dispositions, source traces and decontamination request, then finish for the 13-checkpoint debrief.

checkpoints.description: Inspect all five closed flasks before disposition.
checkpoints.rationale: Visible and clear panels provide different initial evidence; uninspected flasks cannot be dismissed.

checkpoints.description: Use Gram stain for the bacterial pattern and fungal subculture for the fungal pattern.
checkpoints.rationale: Broad category support is useful but does not establish species from appearance.

checkpoints.description: Inspect and quarantine all five linked flasks before any test, disposition or antibiotic intervention.
checkpoints.rationale: Global containment of the linked incident precedes organism or identity naming and prevents interleaved early work while another linked flask remains unquarantined.

checkpoints.description: Obtain dedicated mycoplasma evidence for all three clear flasks before disposition.
checkpoints.rationale: Clear medium, filtration, Gram stain and STR cannot detect or exclude mycoplasma.

checkpoints.description: Order and correctly interpret STR for all three clear flasks.
checkpoints.rationale: Identity evidence requires comparison with a reference and cannot be inferred from labels or morphology.

checkpoints.description: Release only the clear mycoplasma-negative flask with a recorded STR match after review.
checkpoints.rationale: Release needs contamination and identity evidence plus a recorded match; inconclusive or mismatch blocks both identity and authenticated-release checkpoints.

checkpoints.description: Hold the STR-mismatched flask for identity investigation.
checkpoints.rationale: Misidentification requires isolation and investigation rather than use under the old label.

checkpoints.description: Do not use antibiotics as a masking or release pathway.
checkpoints.rationale: Suppressed visible growth is not sterilisation and mycoplasmas resist many routine antibiotics.

checkpoints.rationale: Source tracing weighs lot, equipment, receipt and handling clues against competing hypotheses while remaining distinct from condition assignment and root-cause proof.

checkpoints.description: Hand off all linked flasks with tests, dispositions, traces and decontamination review.
checkpoints.rationale: Complete structured handoff prevents release while evidence and linked risks remain unresolved.

limitations: All organisms, flask assignments, visible panels, assay results, STR loci/alleles, linked-record bundles, source routes and dispositions are synthetic simulation choices; no real register rows, donor profiles, personal data or cell-line data are used.

Simplified assays always return control-valid binary evidence in this exercise; they do not model sensitivity, specificity, non-culturable strains, PCR inhibition/carry-over, mixed profiles or DNA-stain subjectivity.
The four-locus STR table and classroom arithmetic are not a complete ASN-0002 panel or the Tanabe/Masters algorithms. Authentication does not establish sterility, phenotype or reference correctness.
Antibiotic actions never clear quarantine or contamination. No physical manipulation, disinfection effectiveness, organism growth, species identification, rescue efficacy or competency is validated.
